messages.subject_clean: Error in sequenza.extract: Missing values are not allowed in logR input
messages.body_plain:
Thank you Francesco, your solution worked! I have not done the four-part extension yet, as I am trying to devise a way of catching and scripting this process in case it ever needs to be done again. I really appreciate the help.

-Brad

On Friday, May 25, 2018 at 5:27:17 AM UTC-4, Francesco Favero wrote:

> It may not be optimal, but you could skip chromosome 17 for that sample:
>
> sequenza.extract(…, chromosome.list = c(1:16,18:22, "X", "Y”))
>
> I think the problem is the segmentation: if for any reason you know already the segments for that sample you may try to run the function with
>
> sequenza.extract(…, breaks = breakpoints_you_know_already)
>
> if you don’t have breakpoints and you really want chromosome 17 (well, there are a couple of important genes there after all :P), you may try as follow:
>
> 1) run sequenza.extract as I suggested excluding chr 17
> 2) from the segmentation results, take the first 3 columns: chromosome, start, end and save in a object/file (name the columns chrom, start.pos, end.pos)
> 3) open the file/object and manually add a line for chromosome 17 (eg from start to end of the chromosome)
> 4) run sequenza extract with the modified breakpoints
> 5) visual inspect chromosome 17 in the results: if there are other clear breakpoints, you should manually modify the breaks file again and return to point 4
>
> I hope this is not too convoluted, I know it’s very annoying to deal manually with such matters.
>
> Please let me know if you have success in the process!
>
> Francesco
>
>
> > On 22 May 2018, at 16.59, Brad Wubbenhorst <bwubbe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >
> >
> > So this particular sample has a second tumor, but it ran through sequenza without issue. The normal sample used was the same. I am not sure how I can compare them properly to determine what could be the differences in the input.
> >
> > -Brad
> >
> >
> > On Monday, May 21, 2018 at 9:12:13 AM UTC-4, Brad Wubbenhorst wrote:
> > Hi Francesco,
> >
> >    This is the CRAN version. From what I see there were no errors or warnings in the preceding steps for either the tumor or the normal. It does appear that there are little or no heterozygous positions of chromosome 17, or those that are het appear as such:
> >
> > 17      81083158        T       2       72      36.000  0.958   0.042   het     68      72      TC      .       0
> >
> > Is there a way, for now at least, to proceed as if this legitimate? I rely on the CN segments and cellularity estimates for a few other processes. Thank you very much for the help.
> >
> > -Brad
> >
> >
> > On Saturday, May 19, 2018 at 5:42:57 AM UTC-4, Francesco Favero wrote:
> > Hi Brad,
> >
> > Usually this happens in the contigs where the chromosome doesn't have any heterozygous position.
> > Is it possible that either the normal or the tumor have an empty chromosome 17, or something went wrong in the chromosome 17.
> >
> > You might be right about the NA as well. I this the sequenza version in CRAN? or the development from github?
> >
> > Francesco
> >
> >

messages.subject: using alternative solution
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I would like to know if there is an automated way to change the ploidy and cellularity estimate used by sequenza when we run the sequenza.result function. The model fit gives one chosen solution and severals alternative. We have evidences from other sources that seems to point one of the alternate solution as the reality, so I would like to test it.

Thank you

Mathieu

messages.subject: Re: using alternative solution
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mathieu

You can manually set the cellularity and ploidy in the sequenza.results, it will use your solution for the copy number call and in the "view" plots.

Best

Francesco
